sentences.text: Pisanosaurus was a small, ground-dwelling herbivore that could reach about 1 meter in length and weighed approximately 2 kilograms.
Estimates based on the partial skeleton suggest the animal was roughly 1 meter long, 30 centimeters tall, and weighed between 2.5 and 9 kilograms.
The creature possessed an open hip socket, a feature shared with many dinosaurs, though the exact orientation of the pubis bone remains uncertain in reconstructions.
While the tail is reconstructed to be as long as the rest of the body based on other early ornithischians, this view is speculative because the tail has not been recovered.
The only known skeleton was discovered in 1962 by Galileo Juan Scaglia and formally described by Rodolfo Casamiquela in 1967.
The genus name Pisanosaurus honors the Argentine paleontologist Juan Arnaldo Pisano and combines his name with the Greek word saurus meaning lizard.
Fossils were found in the Agua de las Catas locality within the Ischigualasto Formation in La Rioja, Argentina, an area originally dated to the Middle Triassic.
The formation is now believed to belong to the Carnian stage of the Late Triassic, deposited approximately 228 to 216.5 million years ago.
Pisanosaurus lived in a warm, humid environment with seasonal heavy rains and volcanic activity on a volcanically active alluvial plain covered by forests.
The diet likely consisted of ferns, horsetails, and giant conifers.
It was a bipedal animal that was likely herbivorous, like other known ornithischians.
It is hypothesized that the large carnivore Herrerasaurus may have preyed on Pisanosaurus.
In 1993, Sereno noted that Pisanosaurus was found in close association with therapsids, rauisuchians, archosaurs, Saurosuchus, and the dinosaurs Herrerasaurus and Eoraptor.
In 1976, Bonaparte hypothesized that Pisanosaurus played a role in a fauna dominated by therapsids.
The scientific classification of Pisanosaurus has been debated for over 40 years.
A 2008 study identified Pisanosaurus as the earliest and most primitive member of the ornithischian group.
Two independent studies in 2017 concluded that Pisanosaurus was a silesaurid.
The parent group of Pisanosaurus is Parapredentata.
Pisanosaurus lived during the late Triassic period, between 228 and 216 million years ago in the Carnian stage, in what is now South America.
The time range for Pisanosaurus is the Carnian stage, from 233.6 to 227.3 million years ago.
Until 2017, the scientific consensus classified Pisanosaurus as the oldest known ornithischian dinosaur, but more recently some researchers have begun to consider it a non-dinosaurian silesaurid.
Recent studies suggest Pisanosaurus might be a non-dinosaurian silesaurid, but this view has not reached a consensus.
In 1991, Paul Sereno suggested that the Pisanosaurus fossil might be a chimera made of mixed bones.
The classification of Pisanosaurus depends heavily on the debated evolutionary relationships of silesaurids.
A 2015 phylogenetic analysis by Agnolin recovered Pisanosaurus as a possible non-dinosaurian member of Dinosauriformes related to silesaurids.
